articles.title: Oregon’s 1989 dam diverted water to one landowner’s pond; its 2020 removal kept his water right via a pump and reopened 1.8 miles of creek for coho salmon
articles.summary: The removal of a 1989 dam on Kelley Creek, Oregon, has restored migratory paths for coho salmon and maintained water rights for a local landowner through pump technology. This environmental restoration project opens 1.8 miles of vital habitat, promoting biodiversity and sustainable land use.
articles.body: A dam built across Kelley Creek in 1989 in Oregon blocked migrating fish from reaching upstream habitat for three decades while diverting water into a private owner’s pond. The structure was nearly six feet tall, and it reportedly obstructed fish passage through the lower part of the creek, a tributary within the Johnson Creek watershed near Portland. In August 2020, the Johnson Creek Watershed Council (JCWC) removed the dam and substituted its gravity-fed water diversion with a pump, thus allowing the landowner to continue using his water right. 1.8 miles of accessible habitat as the project’s target was identified by the Clackamas Partnership. This was intended to be an opening route that would benefit coho salmon, steelhead and Pacific lamprey. Subsequent environmental DNA observation detected coho salmon at the former dam site, thus providing evidence of their presence extending beyond the barrier.A dam that blocked fish passage for three decadesThe dam was built at river mile 0.5 on Kelley Creek with the intention of holding water upstream and feeding a gravity-powered diversion into an off-channel pond. While the structure served the estateowner’s water needs, the structure spanned the creek and prevented fish like salmon, steelhead and lamprey from migrating into upstream habitat. The Clackamas Partnership classified this as a complete barrier to salmonid passage. Kelley Creek and its tributaries include habitat used by migratory fish, which made the obstruction a priority for restoration efforts in the wider Johnson Creek watershed.In 2015, the planning for fish-passage improvements began. Following this, in 2017, JCWC secured funding from the East Multnomah Soil and Water Conservation District, allowing consultants to explore options for bettering the passage. A 60% engineering design was reportedly completed in November 2018. The team initially considered ways to construct a route that fish could use to bypass the structure. However, when presented with the alternatives, the landowner reportedly suggested removing the dam altogether. That proposal moved the project towards eliminating the barrier while preserving the pond’s water supply.Meanwhile, engineers designed a submersible pump station downstream of the former barrier, near the pond, to replace the gravity-fed diversion. The Clackamas Partnership reported that the Oregon Water Resources Department approved a formal amendment to the water right’s point of diversion and waived the associated processing fee. This pump provided the means of physically drawing water. Therefore, the dam could be removed without requiring the landowner to abandon the existing water use.Removing the barrier and restoring the channelIn August 2020, the removal of the dam was finished. Prior to the demolition, teams slowly lowered the impounded water, exposing mudflats and giving Pacific lamprey buried in the sediment an opportunity to emerge so they could be captured and relocated. This gradual drawdown was aimed at reducing harm to aquatic life during construction. Following the dam’s removal, engineers installed an engineered streambed in the former structure’s footprint to reduce the risk of the channel eroding downwards or cutting sideways into its banks.The replacement water-diversion system also required some changes to the stream channel. Engineers built a riffle downstream to help maintain the pool needed for the pump intake. A screened intake was installed to lessen the risk of fish being drawn into the diversion, while a boulder weir helped direct the flow towards the centre of the pool and keep the screen clear of debris. These features allowed water withdrawal to continue without recreating the original barrier to fish migration.Furthermore, the restoration work included measures to protect the creek beyond the former dam site. According to JCWC, a fence along the stream to prevent livestock from entering the channel was installed alongside plans for riparian revegetation. The department believed that keeping livestock away from the creek can help protect streambanks and newly planted vegetation from trampling. Together, the channel reconstruction and streamside protection measures were intended to improve the stability of the restored reach and support its use by aquatic species.Beyond the former barrier, coho salmon were detectedThe project’s targeted performance measure listed 1.8 miles of accessible stream habitat along Kelley Creek. Its fact sheet identifies coho salmon, steelhead and Pacific lamprey as focal species. In a separate JCWC project documentation in 2020, it was reported that fish passage had been restored to a cumulative total of nearly three miles of Kelley and Mitchell creeks.Subsequent monitoring showed that coho salmon were present at the former dam site. The council’s environmental DNA programme, which analyses genetic material collected from stream water, reported coho salmon DNA at the site where the dam had been removed. The council later noted that coho detections at the site had continued across its sampling efforts.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: ‘$250 protesters’: Trump reacts as hecklers disrupt his rally raising slogans on Epstein - watch
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump was interrupted by two hecklers in quick succession during a rally in Ohio, with one shouting that Trump had travelled on
articles.body: US President Donald Trump was interrupted by two hecklers in quick succession during a rally in Ohio, with one shouting that Trump had travelled on Jeffrey Epstein's plane, prompting the president to accuse the disruptors of being paid protesters.Responding to the heckler, Trump claimed that the man had been paid $250 to disrupt the event and described him as someone following the “radical left playbook”. Trump also brought up his past association with Epstein, the late convicted sex offender, claiming that he had thrown him out of a club around 20 years ago.Trump said: "You know, there's a guy, not a young guy, they gave him $250. Paid Protesters paid. Such. Such losers. Boy, you look at that guy. So that guy, he's right out of the radical left playbook. He's right out of the radical. This guy. This guy was very nondescript. But I will say this. You know, he mentioned Epstein. So I threw Jeffrey Epstein out of a club like 20 years ago because I thought he was a whack job."The interruptions came as Trump addressed the crowd at the Ohio rally. The hecklers' remarks disrupted his speech, prompting him to respond directly to the protesters.Trump has repeatedly alleged, without providing evidence, that people who interrupt his rallies are paid agitators. During the exchange, he also referred to the claim that protesters receive $250 for disrupting his events.In a separate incident reported by the Daily Mail, a heckler interrupted Trump during a rally in Mississippi on Monday, telling him: "Shove that ballroom up your fat a--," in an apparent reference to the planned construction of a new ballroom at the White House.Trump responded by telling the heckler to leave, saying: "Oh, go home," and "Go home, go home."He subsequently claimed that the protesters were being paid, saying: "He gets paid, you know they're paid protesters, they get paid $250 by, they think it's Soros."Trump was referring to billionaire George Soros, a major donor to Democratic and liberal causes. However, the president has not publicly provided evidence to substantiate his claims that the hecklers were paid to disrupt his rallies.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: TVK leader Christopher arrested for sexually harassing college student after offering lift
articles.summary: KANYAKUMARI: A functionary of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) was arrested on Thursday for allegedly sexually harassing a college student after
articles.body: KANYAKUMARI: A functionary of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) was arrested on Thursday for allegedly sexually harassing a college student after offering her a lift home in Tamil Nadu’s Kanyakumari district, police said.Christopher, a member of the party’s central district executive committee, had been absconding since a case was registered against him. He hails from Marundhukottai near Thuckalay.The complainant, a second-year college student from Kulasekaram, studies at a private college in Nagercoil. She regularly travelled with another student from Moolachal, who is also a TVK member, police sources said.On the day of the incident, the two students were waiting for a bus after college when it began raining. Christopher, who knew the other student, stopped his car and offered to drop them home, saying he was travelling in the same direction.After dropping the other student at Moolachal, Christopher continued towards Kulasekaram with the complainant, assuring her that he would drop her near her home, police said.The student alleged that Christopher stopped the vehicle along the way and sexually harassed her. She confronted him and tried to get out of the car to escape, according to police sources. He later dropped her near her residence and fled.The student informed her parents after reaching home and subsequently told her college friend about the incident. The two then approached Thuckalay police station and lodged a complaint.Further investigation is under way.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chennai | Silver Rate in Chennai | Bank Holidays in Chennai | Public Holidays in Chennai | Chennai AQI | Weather in Chennai | Petrol Price in Chennai | Diesel Price in Chennai | CNG Price in Chennai | LPG Price in ChennaiStay updated with the latest Chennai news. articles.title: Pensioners, you can submit your life certificate from home: Who can apply, how it works and the November 30 deadline
articles.summary: Pensioners in India do not have to queue at a bank or pension office to prove they are alive.
articles.body: Pensioners in India do not have to queue at a bank or pension office to prove they are alive. They can generate a Digital Life Certificate (DLC) from home on a smartphone, using the government’s Jeevan Pramaan facility. The service lets pensioners submit their annual life certificate electronically, using Aadhaar-based face authentication without visiting a bank branch. The yearly certificate is what keeps pension payments from being interrupted.Dates and deadline for 2026Presioners who are 80 years old and above can submit their life certificate from October 1 to November 30, 2026. On the other hand, those below 80 years if age canPensioners aged 80 and above can submit their life certificate from October 1 to November submit it from November 1 to November 30. With the November window about to open for most pensioners, anyone who has not yet submitted should plan to do it early and not leave it to the last weekWhat you needFor face authentication, pensioners need an Android smartphone with an internet connection and a suitable front camera. They must download two apps, AadhaarFaceRD and the Jeevan Pramaan Face App. The sources I found describe the process only for Android phones, so iPhone users should check the official Jeevan Pramaan website for their options.The process is also tied to Aadhaar. As per the State Bank of India, the submission of life certificate is an Aadhaar-based process as it helps in the digital authentication and it works only if the account of the pensioner is seeded with their Aadhar number. Before starting the process, the pensioners should check whether their Aadhaar card is linked to their pension account and that the mobile number registered with Aadhaar is active, as the process also requires OTP.How it worksThe steps vary slightly by app version, but the general flow is simple.1. Check your Aadhaar links. The digital life certificate can be authenticated only if your pension account is seeded with your Aadhaar number, and keep your Aadhaar-registered mobile number active for the OTP.2. Use a compatible phone. You need an Android smartphone with an internet connection and a suitable front camera.3. Download the two apps. Install AadhaarFaceRD and the Jeevan Pramaan Face App.4. Open the Jeevan Pramaan app and register. Enter your Aadhaar number and mobile number, then verify with the OTP.5. Fill in your pension details. These include pensioner type, PPO number, bank and disbursing agency.6. Complete face authentication. Capture your face with the phone’s front camera and follow the on-screen instructions.7. Save your Pramaan ID. A unique ID is generated once the process succeeds. You will also get an SMS with a transaction ID.8. Download your certificate. Use the transaction ID at jeevanpramaan.gov.in to download the computer-generated certificate for your records.9. Confirm it was accepted. A successful face scan doesn’t necessarily mean the pension authority has accepted the certificate, so check with your bank or disbursing agency before November 30.Submission is not the same as acceptanceAn important caution is that a successful face scan does not automatically mean the pension authority has accepted the certificate. Business Standard notes that pensioners should visit the Jeevan Pramaan portal after submission and use the Pramaan ID to access their certificate. Pensioners should also keep the ID and SMS, and check with their bank or disbursing agency that the certificate has been recorded before the deadline.If you can’t use a smartphoneNot everyone is comfortable with apps. SBI says a physical life certificate will continue to be accepted if the pensioner prefers it. Other routes include fingerprint or iris devices, the UMANG app, and help at banks, post offices and Common Service Centres. Government campaigns have also run special camps through pension disbursing banks and India Post Payments Bank, and traditional methods remain available for those who cannot access the digital platform. Family members and neighbours can help older pensioners with the smartphone process, but the pensioner must be present for the face scanYou use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Why did Kick suspend Vitaly after his latest livestream? Here’s what we know
articles.summary: Streamer Vitaly has been suspended from Kick after the platform accused him of breaking its rules on endangerment.
articles.body: Streamer Vitaly has been suspended from Kick after the platform accused him of breaking its rules on endangerment. The suspension came on October 28, 2026, while he was working on his “Catching Predators IRL” livestream with rapper Lil Pump. Vitaly shared an email from Kick on X, showing the reason given for the suspension. However, the email did not explain exactly what he did to break the rules. This has left viewers wondering what led to the sudden action against the streamer.What led to Vitaly’s suspension from Kick?Vitaly shared a screenshot of the suspension email he received from Kick. The message said, “Your account has been suspended due to a violation of our Terms of Service and Community Guidelines. Reason for Suspension: Endangerment.”The email also said that screenshots and video recordings were included as evidence. However, Kick did not explain which part of Vitaly’s livestream led to the suspension.The streamer’s Kick channel also became unavailable. People trying to visit the page saw an error message that read, “Oops, something went wrong. We can't find the page you're looking for.”The suspension happened while Vitaly was working on his “Catching Predators IRL” livestream with Lil Pump. However, there is no confirmed information showing that the rapper’s presence or a particular moment from the livestream directly caused the suspension.Kick’s email did not say how long the suspension would last. It is also unclear whether the platform plans to restore Vitaly’s channel or keep it suspended permanently.Vitaly’s Catching Predators livestreams have sparked controversy in the past as well Vitaly’s “Catching Predators” livestreams have faced controversy in the past as well. In April 2026, Vitaly and his team wrongly portrayed Akash Singhania as a child predator during a livestream. Vitaly later apologized publicly and said his team had made a mistake. He also stated that Singhania had been cleared of all wrongdoing.Singhania later spoke about how the incident affected his life. He said the false accusations, along with racism, bullying, and harassment, had caused him serious problems. The incident raised questions about how people are treated during Vitaly’s predator-catching livestreams and the possible harm caused by false accusations.However, there is no link between the April controversy and Vitaly’s latest suspension from Kick. The platform’s email only listed “Endangerment” as the reason for suspending his account.It is also unclear how long the suspension will last or whether Kick will restore Vitaly’s channel. Until the platform or Vitaly provides more details, the exact reason behind the suspension remains unknown.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: ‘This is the future you want?’ White House cites France riots to warn against Democrats ahead of midterms
articles.summary: The White House on Thursday shared a video of violent protest scenes from France, claiming that the unrest could represent their future if they back the
articles.body: The White House on Thursday shared a video of violent protest scenes from France, claiming that the unrest could represent their future if they back the Democratic Party in the November 3 midterm elections.“France before and after is a warning. The chaos, looting, and destruction we’re watching is exactly the future radical Democrats are pushing for America. Is this the future you want?” the White House wrote in a post on X.The post comes amid some of France’s worst unrest in decades, with demonstrations over rising living costs, inequality and deteriorating public services escalating into violence in several cities. The Trump administration has seized on the scenes to criticise immigration policies and portray Democrats as a threat to law and order.France’s protests, however, began with grievances over the country’s education system, including teacher shortages, overcrowded classrooms and poor school facilities, before expanding into wider economic and political discontent. While hundreds of thousands of people took part in demonstrations, violent groups looted shops, attacked police and set buildings and vehicles on fire.What is happening in France?The unrest gathered momentum in September, beginning with student demonstrations over staff shortages and conditions in schools before drawing in teachers, parents, trade unions and other protesters angry about living costs and public spending. The movement also brought together groups opposed to the government’s economic policies, including supporters of the Yellow Vest movement that staged mass protests in 2018.The violence escalated on October 17, when an estimated 550,000 to 800,000 people took part in demonstrations across France. Although most marches were peaceful, some groups looted shops, attacked police and damaged public buildings. Limoges city hall was set on fire, while protesters broke into Marseille city hall and a tourist office in Lyon was torched. Authorities reported around 1,200 arrests and more than 150 injured police officers.What Trump has said on the unrestThe White House’s post follows President Donald Trump’s repeated attempts to link the French unrest to immigration and left-wing politics. A video published by the White House on October 23 combined footage of violence in France with excerpts from Trump’s speech at a rally in Kansas, where he blamed migrants and other groups for the country’s turmoil.The messaging comes just days before the US midterm elections, in which control of Congress is at stake. Trump and other Republicans have invoked the French unrest to argue that Democratic policies could lead to similar disorder in the United States. However, reports on the protests identify school conditions, the cost of living, inequality and public services among the movement’s central grievances, while the violence was concentrated among some groups participating in the wider demonstrations.You use AI every day. articles.title: WhatsApp co-founder Jan Koum donated $36 million to help establish a Los Angeles school campus; on October 25, the new campus opened for grades 9–12, bringing the school's total footprint to 28 acres
articles.summary: A $36 million donation from WhatsApp co-founder Jan Koum has helped a Jewish school in Los Angeles expand its facilities, with a new campus opening for
articles.body: A $36 million donation from WhatsApp co-founder Jan Koum has helped a Jewish school in Los Angeles expand its facilities, with a new campus opening for high school students on Sunday. Milken Community School, which teaches students from grades 6 to 12, has moved its upper school students to the Jan Koum Campus in Bel Air. With the addition of this property, the school now has 28 acres of land spread across three campuses.According to Jewish Journal, the new campus stands at 15600 Mulholland Drive, a property that previously belonged to American Jewish University. It is about half a mile from Milken's two other campuses, known as the Ruby Family Campus and Saperstein Campus. Stephen Wise Temple is located across the street.The school marked the opening with a gathering of families, students, donors and community leaders. According to the Jewish Journal, Israeli singer Ishay Ribo performed at the event, his first appearance before the Milken community. Ribo was the first Israeli artist to headline a concert at Madison Square Garden.WhatsApp co-founder Jan Koum was born on February 24, 1976, into a Jewish family in Kyiv, Ukraine. When he was 16, he moved to California with his mother and grandmother to escape antisemitism and religious persecution in the former Soviet Union.A June 15, 2022, investigation by the Jewish Telegraphic Agency reported that his foundation had donated millions of dollars to Jewish organisations, including approximately $17 million to the European Jewish Association during 2019–2020. The report also noted that Koum had maintained a relatively low public profile regarding his Jewish identity, despite his substantial financial support for Jewish causes.The $36 million donation The property was not always called the Jan Koum Campus. After Milken School co-founder and trustee Lowell Milken acquired it from American Jewish University, it was known as Milken East Campus. The name changed in June 2026, when the school announced a major contribution from the Koum Family Foundation.In a June 18 announcement, Shulkind confirmed that the foundation had committed $36 million towards the school's expansion. The contribution increased the total collected through Milken's capital campaign to $152 million. The school said the fundraising amount was a record in Jewish education.According to Milken Community School's official website, the Koum Family Foundation supports Jewish education and identity-building, works to strengthen the State of Israel and serves Jewish communities around the world. The school said the donation reflected Koum's commitment to supporting Jewish education for future generations.Concerns about antisemitism raised at openingDuring the event, Lowell Milken also addressed the difficulties facing Jewish students and teachers, particularly concerns about increasing antisemitism.He recalled that the school had begun work on the campus a year earlier and said the project was intended to achieve more than the construction of modern classrooms.“For we, as Jews, are living in a time of great challenge, when antisemitism has risen in the nation and the world,” he said as quoted by the Jewish Journal.Milken also spoke about threats to the safety, rights and identity of Jewish students and faculty. He also referred to conspiracy theories and false accusations directed at Jews and Israel.“Milken’s vision is not optional, it is essential and critical,” he said. “To be a beacon for Jewish continuity here and abroad,” he added.The programme also allowed students to participate. Freshman Daliya Eigler sang the US national anthem and “Hatikvah”, while the community choir Makelat Hakehillah performed an arrangement of “Sibat Hasibot”.The expansion of Milken The school's decision to increase its space comes as it reports more families applying for admission. Head of the school Sarah Shulkind told those attending the ceremony that the leadership had chosen to prepare for further growth rather than wait for demand to increase.According to Shulkind, applications this year were 40% higher than the previous year's record figure. She linked this increase to the school's plans to provide more space for Jewish education.The school currently teaches more than 800 students, according to its website. It is an independent, coeducational Jewish day school, with classes covering both middle school and high school grades.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: '$5,000 may not even buy a hamburger': Trump's Mar-a-Lago invitation comes with a pricey twist
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump made a risky joke that the $5,000 payment he has promised Americans would barely cover a hamburger and a small dessert at his
articles.body: US President Donald Trump made a risky joke that the $5,000 payment he has promised Americans would barely cover a hamburger and a small dessert at his Mar-a-Lago resort in Florida, surprisingly drawing laughter and applause from supporters at a campaign rally in Texas.Trump made the remarks at a rally in Corpus Christi on Tuesday, urging supporters to spend the money in the United States rather than overseas. His comments came as the rising cost of living has emerged as a key issue ahead of the November 3 congressional elections. PTI reported.“Go to Florida, go to any one of our great places,” Trump said. “You could even come to Mar-a-Lago. I said it the other night. You’ll be my guest at Mar-a-Lago. The problem is that for USD 5,000, the most you’ll be able to buy is a hamburger and maybe a small dessert. I’m not even sure you could buy that. No, don’t go there. That’s not a good place if you’re price conscious.”The audience, however, responded with laughter and applause rather than taking offence at the joke, suggesting the loyal Maga base the President enjoys.The remarks came amid concerns over affordability, an issue that analysts say could affect the Republicans’ position in Congress.Trump has promised to send cheques worth $5,000 to every American adult if Republicans retain control of both chambers of Congress. The proposal has drawn criticism from Democrats and some supporters of the president, with critics questioning its feasibility and describing it as an attempt to influence voters.The estimated cost of the payments would be USD 1.3 trillion, according to the supplied estimate reported by PTI, and implementing the proposal would require congressional action.The elections on November 3 will determine all 435 seats in the House of Representatives and 35 of the 100 seats in the Senate. Together, the two chambers make up the US Congress, where Republicans currently hold majorities in both.Congressional elections take place every two years. One coincides with the four-year presidential election, while the other is held midway through a president’s term.Republicans currently hold a 53-47 majority in the Senate. Of the 35 seats up for election, Republicans hold 22 and Democrats hold 13. Democrats would need to retain their 13 seats and win four additional seats to secure a majority.In the House of Representatives, Republicans hold 218 seats and Democrats 214, while one seat belongs to an independent. Two seats are vacant.Beyond the congressional races, voters will also elect governors in 36 states. In Ohio, a Republican stronghold, Republican candidate Vivek Ramaswamy is facing Democrat Amy Acton in a closely watched contest.A recent Pew Research Centre study, quoted by PTI, found that 60 per cent of Americans said they did not have enough income to live the life they wanted, while 70 per cent said they had cut back on discretionary spending, including eating out.Trump has continued to maintain that the US economy is performing well and has dismissed concerns about affordability as an issue invented by Democrats.You use AI every day. articles.title: Trump moves to end H-1B visa deference: What it means for Indians stuck in the green-card backlog
articles.summary: For Indian professionals working in the US, an H-1B extension is more than a routine immigration formality.
articles.body: For Indian professionals working in the US, an H-1B extension is more than a routine immigration formality. It is a crucial bridge to maintaining legal status and keeping their path to permanent residency, or a green card, alive as they navigate a backlog that can stretch for decades.Many rely on successive extensions while waiting for their employment-based green cards. A proposed change by the Trump administration could make that process more uncertain, even for workers whose previous visa petitions were approved.The administration has proposed scrapping the US immigration policy known as “deference to prior approvals”. Under the policy, US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) generally gives weight to an earlier favourable decision when reviewing an extension petition involving the same employer, worker and underlying facts, unless certain exceptions apply.The policy requires immigration officers to consider previous approvals, while the proposed change could make it easier for them to reassess a worker’s eligibility.The proposal, published on October 14, is not yet a final rule. If implemented, it could mean closer scrutiny of extension applications from Indian H-1B holders, including those who have spent years building their lives and careers in the US while waiting for employment-based green cards.The change could also affect workers in other visa categories, including L-1 intracompany transfers.Rajiv Dabhadkar, founder of the National Organisation for Software and Technology Professionals (NOSTOPS), told TOI,“Removing deference would not itself change green card queue positions or automatically invalidate existing H-1B approvals. However, it could affect how subsequent petitions are assessed while individuals wait for permanent residency.”Immigration attorney Bhumireddy Sai Srinivas Reddy told TOI the proposal could make the long wait for permanent residency more uncertain for Indian H-1B holders.“For Indian H-1B holders in the EB-2/EB-3 backlog, this rule changes the nature of the green-card wait itself. Most are living on three-year AC21 extensions, four, five, six renewals over a decade. Today each renewal presumes the last approval was correct. Under the proposed rule, every renewal becomes a fresh trial of eligibility, with specialty occupation, wage level, and employer relationship all back on the table,” he said.Indians accounted for about 70 per cent of all H-1B beneficiaries in fiscal year 2025, according to USCIS data, making them a significant group potentially affected by any change to how work visa extensions are adjudicated.What is the US deference policy, and what could change?The US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and USCIS have proposed removing a provision under 8 CFR 214.1(c)(5), which generally requires the agency to give “deference to a prior approval” when adjudicating a request to extend a non-immigrant worker's petition involving the same parties and underlying facts.The DHS explains: “When adjudicating a request filed on Form I-129 (Petition for a Nonimmigrant Worker) involving the same parties and the same underlying facts, USCIS gives deference to its prior determination of the petitioner's, applicant's, or beneficiary's eligibility.”However, deference is not an unconditional guarantee of approval.Under the existing regulation, USCIS can depart from an earlier determination if there was a material error, a material change or new material information that adversely affects eligibility.Employers use Form I-129 to petition for foreign workers in several temporary employment categories, including H-1B, L-1, O-1 and other non-immigrant classifications.If the proposal is finalised, USCIS officers would still be able to consider previous approvals where relevant. However, they would no longer be required to begin from a position of deference to an earlier decision.The proposed change would therefore alter the framework for reviewing extension petitions, rather than automatically changing the basic eligibility requirements for each visa category.How could this affect Indian H-1B professionals waiting for green cards?The proposed change could be particularly consequential for Indian professionals who have spent years working in the US while waiting for employment-based green cards.The H-1B visa allows US employers to hire foreign workers in specialised occupations, with an annual cap of 65,000 visas and another 20,000 for qualifying US advanced-degree graduates.It is generally granted for up to three years and can be extended for another three, with certain workers eligible for extensions beyond the usual six-year limit while pursuing employment-based green cards.For many Indian professionals, the green-card process can stretch over decades because of the high demand for employment-based immigrant visas and country-specific limits on their allocation.A recent analysis by the National Foundation for American Policy (NFAP) estimated that nearly one million Indians are stuck in the US employment-based green-card backlog, accounting for close to 79 per cent of the estimated 1.26 million people waiting in the first three employment-based preference categories.The NFAP analysis also estimated that an Indian professional entering the queue in 2026 could face a potential wait of 179 years in the EB-2 category and 38 years in EB-3, under its modelling assumptions.These projections show the scale of the backlog, although actual waiting periods depend on factors such as visa availability, category and priority date, as well as future policy changes.This would not automatically mean denials, but could increase documentation requirements and uncertainty over processing times.Dabhadkar said, “Additional scrutiny could mean more evidence requests, higher legal and administrative costs, and uncertainty over continued employment, affecting workers’ career decisions and long-term planning.”More scrutiny, additional paperwork for employers?If USCIS officers seek additional evidence, employers may have to submit more detailed documentation relating to job duties, compensation, work locations, business operations, contracts and workers' qualifications.Employers may also need to demonstrate that workers continue to meet the eligibility requirements of their respective visa categories, rather than relying heavily on the fact that an earlier petition was approved.An analysis by the Vasquez Law Firm said the proposal could change how USCIS reviews subsequent petitions.“A worker may feel the practical effects even though the employer is often the petitioner,” the firm noted, explaining that employers may have to document the offered role, business operations, compensation, contracts, work location and the worker's qualifications again.The firm also said workers may need records showing that they have continued to maintain their non-immigrant status.DHS estimates that the proposed rule would impose nearly $133,987 in additional annual costs on petitioners and lead to around 6,044 additional requests for evidence (RFEs) each year.The department says the change could increase adjudication workloads and operational costs as officers spend more time reassessing eligibility and reviewing additional evidence.Reddy said delays caused by additional evidence requests could have consequences for workers whose employment authorisation depends on timely decisions.“The real risk is delay, not denial. More RFEs mean more petitions pending past the 240-day work-authorization window and a worker who hits day 241 must stop working, even with an approved I-140 and a decade of lawful status. With automatic EAD extensions gone, an H-4 spouse's work authorization can lapse in the same queue,” he said.For employers, the consequences could include greater legal and administrative expenses, more time spent preparing extension petitions and less certainty in workforce planning. For workers, additional requests for evidence could prolong the decision-making process.Why does the Trump administration want to end deference?The Trump administration argues that the existing policy could limit the ability of immigration officers to examine applications independently.In its proposal, the DHS said the deference policy may have resulted in “perpetuating erroneous prior approvals and creating an environment in which fraudulent and meritless petitions are less likely to be detected before approval”.The department also argued that some employers may have interpreted the policy as reducing their obligation to show that a worker continues to meet the requirements of the requested visa classification.According to the proposal, the existing regulation effectively shifts the burden from the petitioner to the USCIS officer, who must justify departing from an earlier approval.The DHS says removing the requirement would better align its regulations and adjudication practices with its interpretation of the Immigration and Nationality Act, under which the burden of establishing eligibility for immigration benefits rests with the petitioner.“Removing the deference requirement would also help to ensure that USCIS officers fully review the facts and evidence in every case to ensure continued eligibility,” the proposal states.The policy has changed several times over the years. USCIS first issued guidance on deference in 2004, rescinded it in 2017, and reinstated it in its Policy Manual in 2021. The DHS formally codified the policy in December 2024. The latest proposal would reverse that codification.What happens next?The proposal is open for public comments until November 13, 2026. Interested parties can submit feedback through the federal rulemaking portal, citing DHS Docket No. USCIS-2026-0529.Employers, immigration attorneys, and other stakeholders can use the consultation period to raise concerns about the potential impact on workers and businesses.For Indian professionals, the proposal would change how extension petitions are reviewed, not H-1B eligibility requirements or the existing six-year limit. Current rules remain in effect until a final rule is published and takes effect.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: At 26, Kia Humberstone began building a $40,000 home on a truck to avoid a traditional mortgage after selling her first tiny home for A$35,000, seeking a more affordable path to homeownership
articles.summary: At 26, Kia Humberstone began building a home on the back of a vintage truck and trailer, hoping to find a more affordable path to homeownership without
articles.body: At 26, Kia Humberstone began building a home on the back of a vintage truck and trailer, hoping to find a more affordable path to homeownership without committing to decades of mortgage repayments. Based in Margaret River, Western Australia, she estimated that her second tiny-home project would cost around A$40,000, using recycled materials and her own labour to keep expenses down. Her decision followed an earlier experiment in unconventional living: during the COVID-19 pandemic, she built a tiny home on a truck for A$12,000, lived in it rent-free for two years and later sold it for A$35,000. She used the proceeds to fund a two-year camping trip around Australia. Now, she is building another mobile dwelling to create a home base while retaining the freedom to travel.Why Kia Humberstone chose an alternative to a traditional mortgageHumberstone returned to Margaret River after spending nine months in Sydney, where she became dissatisfied with city life. Having grown up in the countryside, she wanted to return to a simpler lifestyle but found that securing affordable housing remained difficult.She was concerned that taking out a conventional home loan as a single person could leave her making repayments well into retirement. Rather than commit to a mortgage, she decided to build a home herself, aiming to gain greater financial independence and flexibility.Her project reflects a personal response to Australia's housing affordability challenges, particularly for younger people who find it difficult to buy property or secure suitable rental accommodation. Rather than purchasing a conventional house, Humberstone chose to build a mobile dwelling that could serve as her home without being permanently tied to a block of land.She bought a 1988 Isuzu truck for A$5,000For her latest project, Humberstone purchased a 1988 Isuzu truck and trailer for A$5,000. She is converting the vehicle into an approximately 13-metre tiny home, with a projected total cost of around A$40,000.The restoration proved more demanding than she had initially expected. After cleaning the truck, she discovered extensive rust that needed to be removed and treated before construction could progress.Her work included grinding away corrosion, treating the metal, patching holes with fibreglass and sanding the surface in preparation for painting. She was also working towards giving the vehicle a glossy green finish.Once the restoration was complete, the next stage involved installing the walls that would divide the interior into separate living spaces. The project required considerable hands-on work, with Humberstone undertaking much of the labour herself to keep costs manageable.What the A$40,000 tiny home will includeHumberstone planned to turn the truck and trailer into a functional dwelling with four essential areas: a bedroom, bathroom, kitchen and lounge room.The design aims to provide the basic comforts of a conventional home within a compact, mobile structure. Recycled materials are expected to help reduce the overall expenditure, while doing much of the construction herself allows her to avoid some labour costs.At the time of the February 2026 reports, the home was still under construction. Humberstone hoped to move in with the essentials within approximately two months, although she expected the complete project to take another year.The A$40,000 figure is her estimated budget rather than a confirmed final cost. The reports did not establish that the build was completed within that amount.Her first tiny home cost A$12,000 and sold for A$35,000Humberstone had already experimented with truck-based housing during the COVID-19 pandemic, when she built her first tiny home on her parents' property using recycled materials.That project cost approximately A$12,000 and provided her with a place to live without paying rent for two years. She subsequently sold the dwelling for A$35,000, more than twice her original investment.Humberstone used the proceeds to finance a two-year camping trip around Australia. The experience gave her an opportunity to travel while demonstrating how a relatively low-cost housing project could support her preferred lifestyle.Her latest build follows a similar idea, but she intends to create a home base that she can return to between trips. The first project also gave her practical experience of building a dwelling from reused materials and managing a construction project on a limited budget.She is working three jobs to finance the buildHumberstone is funding the new home by working three jobs while carrying out much of the restoration and construction herself. She is also using recyclable materials wherever possible to keep expenses down.The approach demands considerable time and physical effort, from repairing the truck to preparing it for its conversion into a dwelling. Her experience with the first tiny home has given her a starting point, although the second project involves a larger vehicle and an estimated budget of A$40,000.Rather than buying a completed tiny home, she is building one from the vehicle up. This allows her to control the design and work at a pace that fits her available finances, although the final cost will depend on the work and materials required to finish it.Why she chose to build a home on wheelsOne of Humberstone's main reasons for choosing a truck was that she did not own land. A mobile dwelling would give her a place to live without first having to purchase a block of property.She also said that building on a truck offered an alternative to a permanent structure, which she believed would avoid certain council regulations. That is her stated reasoning, rather than confirmation that mobile homes are exempt from planning, parking or other legal requirements in every location.The truck format also fits her plans to continue travelling. Once completed, the dwelling is intended to provide a home base without requiring her to give up the flexibility that has shaped her lifestyle.For Humberstone, the objective is not to replicate a conventional house at a lower price, but to find a way of owning a home that better suits her finances and priorities.Her plan is to live in the home before travelling overseasHumberstone said she hoped to live in the new dwelling for about a year, enjoy the results of her work and potentially rent it out before travelling overseas.She has described the truck home as her future “little home base”, giving her somewhere to return to while continuing to explore other places.The plan combines a relatively low-cost living arrangement with the possibility of generating rental income when she is away. However, the reports describe her intentions at the time of publication and do not confirm whether she subsequently completed the build, moved in or rented out the home.For now, the project represents her attempt to balance homeownership with a lifestyle that leaves room for travel, rather than committing to a conventional mortgage and a fixed property.She hopes to inspire other young people to consider alternative homeownershipHumberstone has been sharing updates about the construction on social media, hoping to encourage other young people, particularly women, to explore alternative routes to homeownership.Her message is that owning a home does not necessarily have to follow the conventional path of purchasing a house with a long-term mortgage. Her own experience includes building a low-cost tiny home, living in it rent-free and selling it to finance travel.Her approach will not suit everyone, and a truck-based dwelling still involves expenses and practical considerations such as where it can be parked, access to utilities, sanitation, insurance and relevant local rules. Nevertheless, her project offers an example of how someone is adapting their housing plans to fit their financial circumstances and preferred way of life.You use AI every day. articles.title: Moon Enters Gemini on Karwa Chauth 2026: These 6 Zodiac Signs May See a Sudden Turn in Fortune
articles.summary: Karwa Chauth falls on Thursday, 29 October 2026, and the Moon spends the whole day in Gemini.
articles.body: Karwa Chauth falls on Thursday, 29 October 2026, and the Moon spends the whole day in Gemini. Fasting women will wait for a waning Moon that is quick, talkative and restless by nature. Gemini is an air sign ruled by Mercury. It favours news, short trips, letters, deals and second thoughts.This year the picture has an extra edge. Uranus, the planet of surprises, is also sitting in Gemini, so the Moon passes very close to it in these hours. Mercury is retrograde in Scorpio. Venus is retrograde too, at the end of Libra. And Mars and Jupiter are moving together through Leo, with the Moon forming a friendly sextile to both. Put simply, the day can bring unexpected openings, though plans may need a second look before they are locked.Six signs feel this shift more strongly than the rest.GeminiThe Moon in your own sign puts you at the centre of attention. A message, a call back or a fresh offer may arrive without warning. Uranus nearby makes you want to act at once. But Mercury, your ruler, is retrograde, so read the fine print twice. Married Geminis may find the evening rituals unusually emotional. A small gesture from a partner can mean more than any gift.LeoFor Leo, the Moon lights up the area of friends, gains and long-held wishes. With Jupiter and Mars both in your sign, support from your circle can turn into something useful. An old contact may suddenly remember you. So keep your phone close. Money matters look brighter than they have in weeks, though big spending should wait until Mercury moves direct.LibraVenus, your ruling planet, is retrograde in your sign, and that has kept some things on hold. Today the Moon forms a soft trine to Venus. Talks that stalled can restart. A delayed travel plan or a pending reply from abroad may finally move. Couples could rediscover an old warmth. Don’t force a decision on property or joint funds, though. Let it settle for a few days.AquariusThe Moon moves through your fifth house of love, children and creative work. Expect a surprise in matters of the heart. Single Aquarians may hear from someone they had almost forgotten. Parents might get good news about a child’s studies or plans. And creative projects get a sudden push. Pluto in your sign adds depth, so feelings that come up today are worth taking seriously.AriesSaturn is retrograde in Aries and has made recent weeks feel heavy. The Gemini Moon gives you a lighter, faster energy. Short travel, paperwork and conversations with siblings carry luck. A quick idea can solve a problem that has dragged on. Speak clearly and avoid sharp words in the evening. Patience pays off better than force right now.VirgoGemini touches your career zone, and Mercury rules both signs. A sudden change at work is possible. It could be a new responsibility, an unexpected meeting or praise from a senior. Some Virgos may get an offer that seemed out of reach. Still, Mercury retrograde suggests checking every detail before saying yes. At home, a quiet word of thanks to elders brings peace.What This Means for EveryoneThe Moon in Gemini makes minds busy on a day that asks for stillness. Fasting can feel tiring when thoughts keep racing. Short prayers, slow breathing and a little silence before moonrise help. Because Venus and Mercury are both retrograde, it’s a better day to repair bonds than to start brand-new commitments. A forgotten promise kept tonight can do more good than a new one made.Get the latest astrology news and horoscope updates. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: Reliance Jio takes biggest share with 1.9 million as India adds 2.2 million subscribers in September
articles.summary: Reliance Jio continued its dominant run across India’s telecommunications sector in September, adding up 1.9 million mobile subscribers (excluding
articles.body: Reliance Jio continued its dominant run across India’s telecommunications sector in September, adding up 1.9 million mobile subscribers (excluding machine-to-machine connections) and capturing the lion’s share of the industry's monthly growth. According to Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) data analysed by brokerages DAM Capital and IIFL Capital, the Indian telecom sector added a net total of 2.2 million mobile subscribers during the month. The expansion lifted the nation’s total wireless subscriber base (excluding M2M connections) to 1.155 billion, marking a year-on-year addition of 22.8 million users.Jio pulls ahead Airtel and ViJio’s September performance mirrored its August numbers. The telecom giant added 1.9 million core mobile users, taking its total mobile base to approximately 483 million. On an annual basis, Jio has added 17.4 million users.For Bharti Airtel, net additions dropped to 200,000, bringing its total mobile base to 406 million. Its year-on-year growth stood at 13.3 million. Vodafone Idea (Vi) continued to bleed users, with underlying losses widening to 300,000 (260,000 based on IIFL Capital's specific breakdown) compared to a loss of 140,000 in August.State-run BSNL maintained positive momentum, adding roughly 500,000 mobile subscribers for the second consecutive month, cushioning Vi's losses and lifting total industry tallies.Jio vs Airtel vs Vi: Active subscriber gainsThe gap between operators grew even more apparent in Visitor Location Register (VLR) data, which measures active network connections. Jio gained 1.3 million active VLR subscribers during September; in contrast, Airtel shed 200,000 active users, while Vodafone Idea lost 300,000. Across the entire telecom landscape, the core VLR base expanded by 600,000.When it comes to wired and fixed-broadband, Jio also outpaced Airtel, adding roughly 400,000 connections in September compared to Airtel’s 200,000. India's total home broadband base grew by 600,000 to reach 68.1 million users, though both operators experienced a mild slowdown from the monthly additions of over one million recorded in prior periods.You use AI every day.
